excerpt: QuestDB is an open-source time-series database built for low-latency ingestion and SQL queries, with a paid Enterprise edition. Free under Apache 2.0.
content:
QuestDB is a time-series database: a database designed for data that arrives as a stream of timestamped events, such as market ticks, sensor readings or application metrics. Its website says it ingests millions of events per second, computes on live data in milliseconds and keeps years of history, queried with ordinary SQL. Newer versions store older data as Parquet files on object storage, so one query can span recent "hot" data and cheaper "cold" storage. The company says it began in electronic foreign-exchange trading, that its core is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence, and that it is used in production at tier-1 banks. Its site shows about 17,300 stars on GitHub.

QuestDB's about page gives 2019 as its founding year. Nicolas Hourcard is co-founder and CEO and Vlad Ilyushchenko is co-founder; in a company blog post, Hourcard wrote that he met Ilyushchenko at a fintech startup, where Ilyushchenko had been building the project for five years. TechCrunch reported that QuestDB went through Y Combinator's summer 2020 batch.

Funding

In November 2021 QuestDB announced a $12 million Series A from 468 Capital and Uncorrelated Ventures, with angels including Alexis Ohanian; TechCrunch said that brought total funding to $14.3 million, including a $2.3 million seed round in 2020.

Pricing

QuestDB open source is free to download and run under the Apache 2.0 licence. QuestDB Enterprise adds high availability with replication and automatic failover, single sign-on, role-based access control and audit logs, tiered storage to Parquet, deployment on cloud, on-premises or in your own cloud account, and SLA-backed support. Enterprise prices are not published; there is a free Enterprise trial and a contact-sales form.

Who it suits

QuestDB suits engineers in trading, crypto, energy, IoT and observability who need fast ingestion and SQL over large volumes of time-stamped data. Teams with ordinary transactional data will be better served by a general-purpose database.

We have not benchmarked QuestDB. This page is based on its website, enterprise and about pages (checked 15 October 2026), its blog and TechCrunch.
